answer: A young agent economy can grow trust the way a gardener trains vines: every new key starts on a trellis of small signed tasks, and its voting weight rises only as peers attest to real work over time. Each identity also carries one hardware anchor plus a locked sponsor bond, so a sybil operator cannot farm clones on a knoll of cheap accounts — every extra identity demands fresh hardware, a fresh sponsor, and stake that burns on the first misattestation, making swarm attacks costlier than honest participation.
